description: DEF CON 33 Community Stage features presentations on mentorship, digital privacy, grassroots movements, and community-driven security defense. Sessions cover declarative dependency management with Nix, agentic AI security, game hacking parallels to offensive red teaming, and counter-surveillance strategies.

talks.title: Access to Secure Dependency Management Everywhere with Nix
talks.teaser: Explores how Nix and NixOS provide reproducible software builds, declarative dependency management, and SBOM traceability across homelabs and enterprise environments.
talks.summary:
The Growing Need for Reproducible Software Environments

Modern software deployment faces persistent challenges from unwanted application updates, third-party cloud data harvesting, and Docker image bitrot. Declarative package management offers a reproducible alternative for self-hosting.

Declarative Package Management with Nix and Nixpkgs

Tom Berek, Farid Zakaria, and D Baker explain how Nixpkgs—spanning over 120,000 Linux packages—enables deterministic builds, precise dependency isolation, and atomic system rollbacks across diverse architectures.

Software Supply Chain Traceability and SBOMs

Nix provides complete traceability of build inputs and dependency hashes, automatically generating verifiable Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) without manual auditing.

Reclaiming Software Sovereignty in Homelabs

Deploying Nix and NixOS in self-hosted homelabs empowers users to maintain software independence, escape vendor lock-in, and build secure, long-lasting computing environments.

talks.title: Securing Agentic AI Systems and Multi-Agent Workflows
talks.teaser: Presents threat modeling and defensive guardrails for autonomous multi-agent AI workflows, covering persistent memory, tool execution, and prompt injection.
talks.summary:
The Shift from AI Copilots to Autonomous Agents

Artificial intelligence architectures are rapidly transitioning from single-turn copilots to autonomous multi-agent systems that coordinate complex actions across persistent memories, API tools, and downstream databases.

Expanded Attack Surfaces in Multi-Agent Workflows

Andra Lezza and Jeremiah Edwards analyze novel attack vectors in agentic ecosystems, including indirect prompt injection at scale, malicious tool invocations, and compromised inter-agent messaging pipelines.

Implementing Policy-as-Code Guardrails

Securing autonomous workflows requires deploying policy-as-code guardrails, strict least-privilege API permissions, and continuous behavioral anomaly detection across agent execution chains.

Red Teaming and Defensive Blueprints

Case studies demonstrate practical red-teaming methodologies for autonomous assistants and provide defensive blueprints to harden agentic pipelines without hindering developer innovation.

talks.title: Passing the Torch: Mentoring and Protecting Our Students
talks.teaser: Educators share practical strategies for building student helpdesk programs, cybersecurity clubs, and mentorship pipelines to inspire the next generation of hackers.
talks.summary:
The Vital Role of Mentorship in Technology

Early mentorship and welcoming communities play a pivotal role in guiding young people toward rewarding careers in technology, cybersecurity, and engineering.

Building Technology and Security Cultures in Schools

Navaar Johnson and Sam Comini discuss their experiences fostering student-led IT helpdesks, cybersecurity clubs, and competitive eSports teams within their school district.

Overcoming Barriers to Student Engagement

Creating inclusive spaces for hands-on technical learning empowers students from all backgrounds to develop practical problem-solving skills and ethical computing habits.

Empowering the Next Generation of Hackers

The panel encourages conference attendees to get involved in local educational mentorship, share industry expertise, and build supportive pipelines for aspiring security practitioners.

talks.title: Private, Private, Private: Access Everywhere
talks.teaser: Demonstrates practical OSINT techniques to audit personal digital footprints and hands-on obfuscation methods to minimize public data exposure.
talks.summary:
Balancing Public, Private, and Secret Lives

In an era where personal information is commodified and accessible across the internet, actively managing digital footprints is essential to preserving individual autonomy and privacy.

Auditing Personal Digital Footprints via OSINT

Meghan Jacquot walks attendees through practical open-source intelligence (OSINT) workflows to map out publicly exposed personal information, public records, and social media data.

Actionable Data Minimization and Obfuscation

Implementing browser privacy protections, opting out of data broker aggregators, and adopting aliases reduce digital exposure and protect against identity theft.

Cultivating Everyday Operational Security

Developing consistent privacy habits empowers individuals to navigate connected services securely while maintaining control over their personal data.

talks.title: So You Want to Make a Badge? Badge Creation 101
talks.teaser: Security engineer Jeff Geisperger introduces the fundamentals of electronic conference badge design, PCB fabrication, and badgelife hardware hacking.
talks.summary:
Hardware hacker and maker Jeff Gisberger ("Big Taro") delivers a comprehensive beginner's guide to custom conference badge design and electronics manufacturing on the Community Stage [00:02]. Gisberger covers the foundational workflow of badge creation, explaining how to transition from circuit concepts to printed circuit board (PCB) layouts using Electronic Design Automation (EDA) suites like KiCad [05:47].

The talk details the popular Shitty Add-On (SAO) standard for modular badge peripherals, exploring creative design choices involving component selection, multilayer FR4 routing, soldermask colors, and decorative silkscreen graphics [05:49, 11:16]. Gisberger shares practical advice on breadboarding prototypes, choosing suitable microcontrollers (such as the ESP32 or RP2040), and integrating display screens [16:46, 22:17]. He highlights interactive features from prior community badges—including playable Frogger games and custom BLE scanners configured to alert wearers to nearby Bluetooth MAC addresses [27:48]—encouraging attendees to participate in the Badge Life hardware community.

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Game Hacking 101
talks.teaser: Julian Dunning introduces core video game security principles, memory inspection concepts, and reverse engineering fundamentals for aspiring game hackers.
talks.summary:
Hardware Hacking and Physical Security

This talk covers hardware hacking techniques and physical security analysis. Topics include circuit board analysis, side-channel attacks, firmware extraction, and low-level debugging of hardware systems.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: DDoS: The Next Generation
talks.teaser: Explores the future of Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack vectors, dynamic amplification techniques, and emerging mitigation architectures.
talks.summary:
This DEF CON talk covers ddos: the next generation.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: How Nation-State Hackers Turn Human Error into Catastrophic Failures
talks.teaser: Analyzes real-world breaches in research laboratories and manufacturing facilities to examine how nation-state actors exploit human error and misconfigurations.
talks.summary:
Nation-State Threats to Critical Infrastructure

State-sponsored Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) groups strategically target research laboratories, manufacturing plants, and industrial control networks to exfiltrate intellectual property and disrupt operations.

Analyzing Attack Vectors in Three Case Studies

N Case and J McCoy present forensic case studies of nation-state intrusions, analyzing how attackers chain social engineering lures, credential theft, and minor system misconfigurations into catastrophic breaches.

Exploiting Human Vulnerabilities and Inadequate Controls

Adversaries routinely capitalize on routine human errors—such as unpatched test systems, shared credentials, and ignored alerts—to bypass perimeter defenses.

Strengthening Organizational Defenses

Mitigating sophisticated nation-state attacks requires continuous threat hunting, tiered identity management, and fostering a blameless security culture focused on rapid error detection.

talks.title: Defending Reddit at Scale
talks.teaser: Explores Reddit's defense architecture and custom in-house resiliency engineering designed to handle massive traffic spikes and sophisticated platform abuse.
talks.summary:
Scaling Defense on High-Traffic Social Platforms

Reddit serves hundreds of millions of active users, creating massive traffic volumes and attracting persistent abuse, credential stuffing, and volumetric network attacks.

Custom Traffic Analysis and Behavioral Filtering

Pratik Lotia and Spencer Koch detail how Reddit engineers tailored in-house traffic analysis pipelines to detect automated scraping and abusive bot networks in real time.

Architectural Resiliency and Adaptive Throttling

Deploying distributed caching layers, dynamic rate-limiting algorithms, and fault-tolerant cloud microservices ensures platform availability during unexpected viral events and coordinated attacks.

Lessons for High-Scale Infrastructure Defense

Building resilient defense systems at scale requires close collaboration between security and platform engineering teams, continuous chaos testing, and adaptive telemetry pipelines.

talks.title: Tunnelpocalypse
talks.teaser: Rich Compton explores a critical network routing and IP spoofing vulnerability that enables global DDoS amplification attacks across tunneling protocols.
talks.summary:
In this network security presentation from the DEF CON 33 Community Stage, DDoS mitigation engineer Rich presents "Tunnelpocalypse," an investigation into protocol encapsulation vulnerabilities that threaten modern internet routing. Opening at 00:00, Rich describes the operational hazards of handling massive volumetric denial-of-service attacks across high-speed enterprise networks.

At 05:01, he dives into the core vulnerability: unvalidated IP-in-IP, GRE, and IPv6 tunneling configurations on core transit routers. He demonstrates how remote adversaries forge outer packet headers, allowing spoofed packets to slip past edge firewall rules and terminate directly inside protected network segments. At 10:02, he references global telemetry gathered in collaboration with The Shadowserver Foundation, illustrating widespread router exposure across global transit providers.

At 15:00, Rich demonstrates packet reflection and amplification attacks enabled by misconfigured tunnel endpoints. He closes at 20:02 by urging network operators to implement rigorous edge Access Control Lists (ACLs), enforce BCP 38 / RFC 2827 ingress source address filtering, and patch routing firmware to ensure encapsulated traffic cannot bypass perimeter security boundaries. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: What Game Hackers Teach Us About Offensive Security & Red Teaming
talks.teaser: Joe Aurelio draws parallels between video game cheat loaders and enterprise malware, exploring how anti-cheat countermeasures mirror modern EDR evasion tradecraft.
talks.summary:
An offensive security researcher explores the technical synergies between commercial game cheating and enterprise red teaming on the Community Stage, demonstrating how game hackers consistently pioneer evasive techniques later adopted by advanced malware authors [00:01, 04:10]. The speaker illustrates that while fundamental exploitation concepts remain consistent, the rapid cat-and-mouse dynamic between cheat developers and anti-cheat systems drives cutting-edge evasion research.

The presentation analyzes low-level evasion techniques, including in-memory code execution, Direct Memory Access (DMA) hardware attacks, and stealthy memory manipulation designed to leave zero forensic artifacts upon termination [08:21]. The speaker details behavioral evasion strategies, such as developing aimbots that bypass algorithmic detection by emulating physical hardware mouse movements through simulated controller curves rather than direct memory writes [12:54]. The session concludes with a deep dive into kernel-level warfare, examining how game hackers bypass UEFI Secure Boot, exploit vulnerable signed third-party drivers (BYOVD), and operate custom hypervisors beneath Ring 0 anti-cheat engines [20:45, 25:21].

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: ReclaimTech: A Community Movement
talks.teaser: Tech Reclaimers founders introduce a grassroots community movement promoting digital sovereignty, peer-to-peer alternatives, and ethical technology adoption.
talks.summary:
Challenging Extractive Big Tech Ecosystems

Modern digital life is increasingly dominated by monopolistic tech platforms and venture-backed services that monetize user data and lock users into proprietary walled gardens.

The Philosophy of Tech Reclaimers

Janet Vertesi and Andy Hull introduce ReclaimTech, a community-driven movement of conscientious objectors working to restore individual autonomy and digital sovereignty.

Building Peer-to-Peer Support Networks

Rather than advocating for extreme digital minimalism, ReclaimTech focuses on meeting people where they are, providing step-by-step guidance to adopt open-source, ethical, and self-hosted tools.

Fostering a Community for a Better Tech Future

Cultivating collaborative local support networks enables individuals to regain control of their data while building meaningful connections with like-minded peers.

talks.title: Cybersecurity in Latin America: Stories of Resilience & Innovation
talks.teaser: Giovanni Forero shares stories of adaptation, community resilience, and grassroots innovation among cybersecurity defenders across Latin America.
talks.summary:
Social Engineering and Human-Oriented Security

This presentation explores social engineering attacks and human vulnerability in security systems. Topics include psychological manipulation, pretexting, credential harvesting, and how attackers exploit human nature to bypass technical defenses.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: OSINT Enabled Ghost Mode: Counter Surveillance for Everyday People
talks.teaser: Cybersecurity architect Desiree Wilson outlines proactive counter-surveillance strategies and OSINT methodologies to protect personal privacy in daily life.
talks.summary:
This presentation focuses on reconnaissance and open-source intelligence gathering methodologies.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)
